native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the hundred-year-slice PCA on forms of capital, the symbolic-capital variables — hatchet/sword (PC1 +0.299, PC2 +0.054), dagger (PC1 +0.266, PC2 +0.074) and house size (PC1 +0.225, PC2 +0.327) — load positively with tight, moderate, near-equal values on PC1 (range 0.074), forming a coherent symbolic-capital block that co-varies with, but does not dominate, the axis (top PC1 loadings: copper/gold +0.407, pottery decoration +0.382, depot +0.340). Across PC2 the group fans out: hatchet/sword and dagger load near zero and stay paired (Δ 0.020), while house size loads distinctly higher (+0.327; trio PC2 range 0.273), making house size the outlier carrying the group's PC2 expression. PC1 explains 30.3% and PC2 19.5% of variance; PC1 scores peak in later slices (c. 1400-1000 BCE).
